content_preview.title: X.Org Server Reaches Second Release Candidate for 26.1, Its First Major Update Since 2021
content_preview.summary: X.Org Server's second 26.1 release candidate landed September 9, alongside a companion Xwayland RC, nearly five years after the project's last major tagged release.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

X.Org Server, the display server software that has underpinned Linux desktops for decades, published a second release candidate for version 26.1 on September 9, moving the project closer to what would be its first major tagged release since X.Org Server 21.1 debuted in October 2021, according to [Phoronix](https://www.phoronix.com/news/X.Org-Server-26.1).

editor_notes.source_verification: Read all four source snapshots in full from sources/2026-09/xorg-server-reaches-second-release-candidate-for-261-its-first-major-update-since-2021/ after verifying each file's sha256 against manifest.json (all four matched: source-0 through source-3). (1) source-0.html.gz (phoronix.com/news/X.Org-Server-26.1) — the fetched page renders as the Phoronix homepage/news-feed (its <title> is the generic site title, not the article headline), which is how Phoronix's short-form 'news flash' URLs behave; the specific item 'X.Org Server 26.1 Moves Closer To Release As Half-Decade Update' (10 September, 41 Comments) appears within that feed and contains the exact quoted text used in the article — 'the first new tagged feature release since X.Org Server 21.1 debuted back in October 2021' and 'new features, many code reverts, and many bug fixes merged over the past five years' — both verbatim matches. This is a structural quirk of Phoronix's site, not a sourcing failure: the cited claims are present and verbatim. (2) source-1.html.gz (mail-archive.com msg01950, rc1 announcement) — confirms Alan Coopersmith's Aug 19, 2026 rc1 announcement, verbatim quotes 'Removal of autoconf/automake build system, leaving only meson', 'Disallow byte-swapped clients by default', and 'against libpciaccess 0.19 (released in March 2026)', and the list of legacy tools (Xorg, Xephyr, Xnest, Xvfb, Xwin, Xquartz) the article paraphrases accurately. (3) source-2.html.gz (mail-archive.com msg01952, rc2 announcement) — confirms Alan Coopersmith's Sept 9, 2026 rc2 announcement text verbatim, the tag xorg-server-26.0.99.902, and every attributed commit/quote in the article: Jeremy Huddleston Sequoia's 'RegionValidate: Fix double free of badreg->data on the error path' and multiple xkb group-count guard commits; Daniel Monteiro's failed-GPU-screen-not-fatal fix; Ivaylo Dimitrov's DPMS fix quoting 'when timeouts are disabled' verbatim; Ben Song's cursor fix quoting 'save cursor in master's sprite_priv instead of slave's' verbatim. Counted exactly nine named contributors in the shortlog (Alan Coopersmith, Ben Song, Daniel Monteiro, Ivaylo Dimitrov, Jeremy Huddleston Sequoia, Lukáš Lipinský, Matthieu Herrb, Olivier Fourdan, stefan11111), matching the article's 'nine contributors' claim exactly. (4) source-3.html.gz (mail-archive.com msg01951, Xwayland rc2 announcement) — confirms Olivier Fourdan's Sept 9, 2026 announcement, quoted verbatim: 'the second release candidate of the upcoming standalone Xwayland 26.1.0 release (or Xwayland 26.1.0 rc2 for short)'; same-day timestamp as the xorg-server rc2 (both Sept 9) supports the article's 'announced separately the same day' framing.
